query: Between 2015 and 2019, did Kenya's economy get more or less nominal income out of each shilling of broad money, and by what percentage did that ratio change?

text.text: Identifies the applicable approach: income velocity of money, i.e. nominal GDP divided by the broad money stock (equivalently 100 divided by broad money as a percent of GDP); change over time = nominal income growth relative to money growth.
text.accept: full = names income velocity / GDP-to-broad-money turnover and uses nominal GDP over M2; partial = reports only M2/GDP without the inversion; no = unrelated approach (money multiplier, seigniorage, credit gap).

data.text: Retrieves the input series: NY.GDP.MKTP.CN, FM.LBL.BMNY.CN.
data.accept: full = all inputs retrieved with values close to the frozen ones; partial = some; no = none.

computation.text: Income velocity changes by about 12.5 percent between 2015 and 2019 (from 2.335 to 2.627).
computation.accept: full = within +/-1.0 percentage point of 12.47; partial = within +/-3 points; no = otherwise.

targets.name: value
targets.tolerance_source: identity recomputed from frozen WDI; rounding and vintage

answer.text: Velocity rose (broad money grew slower than nominal income).
answer.accept: full = correct direction; no = wrong direction.

grading.note: Definition: velocity = nominal GDP / broad money (both LCU). Tolerance 3 percent of level, 1.0 pp for changes.

provenance.validation: recompute with scripts/mo_build.py; WDI ratio consistency checked on 8,360 country-years, 0 mismatches above 0.5

method_doc_cite: WEO April 1985, p.130 (Chart 2-2): "Narrow and Broad Money Velocity (Quarterly GNP at annual rates/average stock of money during quarter)"; p.131-132 relate target money growth to expected nominal GDP growth to get the implied change in velocity.
distractors: Financial depth ratio read on its own (M2 to GDP) without turning it into turnover
